Daily Life and Free Time

Describe your routine, your free time and your favourite places, and compare the past with today — the complete IELTS Speaking test.

Level: A2
Exam focus: Speaking Parts 1–3
Mock: Full test · 11–14 min
Class: 60 minutes
1
Warm-up

A day in Mariana's life

5 min

Mariana is a chef from Portugal. She works in a restaurant in Leeds. Look at her working day.

Task 1

Look at the timeline. Choose the answer.

  1. What time does Mariana start work?
  2. How does she go to work?
  3. When is she busiest?
  4. What does she do after work?
  5. How many hours does she sleep, more or less?
Talk to your teacher: What does a normal day look like for you? What is the busiest part? (Use: I usually… At about… Then…)
2
Grammar

How often? Routines and changes

12 min

A · Frequency adverbs

RuleExample
before the main verbI usually get up at 6:30. She never drinks coffee.
after the verb beI'm always tired on Fridays. The bus is often late.
questionsDo you often cook? · How often do you go to the gym?
longer expressions go at the endI go swimming once a week / twice a month / every Sunday.
Exercise 1

Choose the correct sentence.

  1. usually
  2. always
  3. never
  4. once a week
  5. often

B · Present simple or present continuous?

Present simplePresent continuous
routines and things that are always truenow, at this moment — or a temporary situation
I work in a restaurant.I'm working late this week (only this week).
She takes the bus every day.She's taking a taxi today because it's raining.
Exercise 2

Choose the correct form.

  1. I ______ to work by bus every day.
  2. Sorry, I can't talk now — I ______ dinner.
  3. Mariana usually ______ at 4:30.
  4. This month I ______ English every evening for my exam.
  5. Look! It ______ again.
  6. How often ______ you go to the cinema?
3
Vocabulary + pronunciation

Daily routine and free time

10 min

Study the 12 words. Press 🔈 to hear each word and the example sentence.

get upphrasal verb
Leave your bed in the morning.
I get up at half past six.
commutenoun / verb
The journey to and from work.
My commute takes forty minutes.
have lunchverb phrase
Eat in the middle of the day.
I have lunch at two o'clock.
finish workverb phrase
Stop working for the day.
I finish work at half past four.
do the shoppingverb phrase
Buy food and things for the house.
I do the shopping on Saturdays.
work outphrasal verb
Do exercise, for example at the gym.
I work out three times a week.
go for a walkverb phrase
Walk for pleasure.
We go for a walk by the river.
meet friendsverb phrase
See your friends.
I often meet friends for lunch.
stay inphrasal verb
Stay at home in the evening.
On Fridays I usually stay in.
hobbynoun
Something you enjoy doing in your free time.
My hobby is photography.
relaxverb
Rest and feel calm.
I relax with a good book.
recharge your batteriesidiom
Rest so you have energy again.
I need a holiday to recharge my batteries.
Exercise 3

Choose the correct verb.

  1. I ______ the shopping on Saturday mornings.
  2. We ______ for a walk after lunch.
  3. I ______ lunch at about two o'clock.
  4. I ______ out at the gym three times a week.
  5. On Friday evenings I usually stay ______ and watch a film.
  6. My ______ to work takes forty minutes.

Pronunciation · three sounds for -s

With he, she, it, the verb ends in -s. It has three sounds. Press 🔈 to listen.

SoundAfter…Examples
/s/p, t, k, fworks · gets · takes
/z/most other soundsplays · goes · listens
/ɪz/ — an extra syllables, z, sh, ch, x, gefinishes · watches · relaxes

4
Exam strategy

Organising a 2-minute talk

8 min
Start

Say what you'll talk about

I'm going to talk about… / I'd like to describe…

Middle

Follow the card

One part for each line of the card. Add a detail or an example to each.

Why?

Make it the longest part

The main reason is… · Another reason is… · Also…

End

Finish clearly

So, that's why… · So for me, it's the perfect…

!

In Part 3, the examiner often asks you to compare the past and now. Useful frame: Twenty years ago, people… Nowadays, … On the other hand, …

Exercise 5

What does each phrase do?

  1. “I'm going to talk about…”
  2. “The main reason is…”
  3. “So, that's why I love it.”
  4. “Twenty years ago… Nowadays…”
  5. “For example, …”
Exercise 6

Choose the better Part 3 answer.

  1. Examiner: Do people have enough free time today?
  2. Examiner: Is it important for adults to have hobbies?

Practice test

IELTS Speaking · full test

Time: 11–14 minutes · Use headphones and a quiet room.

  1. The examiner asks a question. Answer out loud, then press Next question.
  2. In Part 2 you get 1 minute to prepare (make notes on paper) and up to 2 minutes to speak.
  3. Your whole test is recorded. At the end you can listen to it and download it for your teacher.
  4. Allow the microphone when your browser asks.
Part 1 · InterviewPart 2 · Long turnPart 3 · DiscussionFinished
HC
Examiner · Helen Carter
…

Describe a place you like to visit in your free time.

You should say:
  • where it is
  • how often you go there
  • what you do there
and explain why you like it.
Good morning. My name is Helen Carter. Can you tell me your full name, please?
And what shall I call you?
And can you tell me where you're from?
Thank you. Now, in this first part, I'd like to ask you some questions about yourself. Let's talk about your daily routine. What time do you usually get up?
What's the busiest part of your day?
Is your routine different now from when you were a child?
Let's move on to talk about weekends. What do you usually do at the weekend?
Do you prefer busy or relaxing weekends?
Did you do anything special last weekend?
Now let's talk about hobbies. Do you have a hobby?
Is there a hobby you would like to try in the future?
Now I'm going to give you a topic, and I'd like you to talk about it for one to two minutes. Before you talk, you'll have one minute to think about what you're going to say. You can make some notes if you wish. Here's your topic. I'd like you to describe a place you like to visit in your free time.
Alright? Remember you have one to two minutes for this, so don't worry if I stop you. I'll tell you when the time is up. Can you start speaking now, please?
Thank you. Do you usually go there alone or with other people?
We've been talking about a place you like to visit in your free time, and I'd like to discuss with you one or two more general questions related to this. Let's consider first of all free time today. Do you think people have enough free time today?
How has the way people spend their free time changed in the last twenty years?
Is it important for adults to have hobbies? Why?
Finally, let's talk about work. Should companies give their workers more holidays?
Thank you. That is the end of the speaking test.
Exam script

A full Speaking test — examiner and candidate

Mariana, a chef from Portugal, takes the test. Her answers are at about Band 6 — a good model to aim for. Listen, read, and turn on the teacher notes to see what makes each answer good.

Marking guide

How Speaking is marked

Four criteria, each worth 25%. Simplified guide for bands 4–7 — see the official public band descriptors on ielts.org for the full wording.

BandFluency & coherenceVocabularyGrammarPronunciation
7Speaks at length without effort; good linking.Flexible; some less common words and idioms.A range of complex sentences; frequent error-free sentences.Easy to understand; good stress and intonation.
6Willing to speak at length; some repetition or self-correction.Enough words to discuss topics; can paraphrase.Simple and complex sentences; errors rarely block meaning.Generally clear; some sounds unclear at times.
5Keeps going but slowly; repeats; simple linking.Manages familiar topics.Basic sentences fairly accurate.Understandable, with some mispronunciation.
4Long pauses; cannot keep going without help.Basic words; frequent mistakes.Basic sentences; many errors.Often difficult to understand.

Teacher: mark the student's recording

Examiners give a whole band (0–9) for each criterion. Choose one for each; the Speaking band is calculated.

Fluency & coherence
Vocabulary
Grammar
Pronunciation
Speaking band
—
Average of the four criteria, rounded to the nearest half band (an approximation of the official method).

Teacher notes — lesson timing

00–05 Timeline + Task 1; students describe their own day.
05–15 Frequency adverbs (Ex 1); simple vs continuous (Ex 2).
15–23 Routine collocations (Ex 3); -s endings (Ex 4) — drill aloud.
23–28 2-minute talk structure; phrases (Ex 5); Part 3 answers (Ex 6).
28–43 Mock test with the simulator — the student records the whole test.
43–60 Listen to the recording together; mark it; compare with Mariana's script.
!

Watch for: adverb position (I go usually); missing -s (she work); present simple for temporary actions; stopping Part 2 after one minute.

Homework (about 45 minutes)

  1. Listen to Mariana's test twice. Copy 5 sentences with frequency adverbs into your notebook. (10 min)
  2. Record your answers to the 11 Part 1 questions in the simulator — use a frequency adverb in each answer. (15 min)
  3. Part 2: one minute of notes, then two minutes: Describe a hobby you enjoy. Record it and listen: did you cover every line? (10 min)
  4. Pronunciation: say 10 verbs with he/she and sort them into /s/, /z/ and /ɪz/. (10 min)
